messages:
marta: Quick question — for the rekeying plan I'm drafting: what's the practical DEK refresh cadence we want? Is it time-based (e.g., 90d), usage-based (rotate after N unwrappings), or both? Also thinking about KMS call load if every unwrap hits KMS during traffic spikes.

tyler: I'd do hybrid. Default rotate 90d, but also force on suspect compromise. For unwrapping, cache DEKs in an in-memory LRU with ttl that depends on request rate (hot keys live longer). Avoid synchronous KMS calls on tail latency.

amanda: Agree. Also recommend a short-lived shard-local cache plus a global warmup step on deploys: when a new DEK is promoted, pre-warm the cache with a sampling of prefixes to avoid cold thundering herd.

marta: How do we surface audit logs for these pre-warm unwraps? We want to prove to auditors that pre-warm calls are authorized system activity, not user access.

tyler: Add a 'reason' and 'actor' field to the KMS request metadata and write an audit_event to internal audit service. KMS logs will still show a decrypt/unwrapping call; correlate by trace id. For AWS KMS you can include GrantTokens? But better to use CloudTrail + our audit event.

amanda: Proposed metrics: `kms_unwrap_count`, `kms_unwrap_latency_ms`, `dek_cache_hits`, `dek_cache_misses`, `dek_cache_evictions`, and a `kms_call_sample_rate` label so we can trace samples to logs. Also emit a 'prewarm' label on audit events.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: services/encryptor v3.14 deployed by @tyler at 2024-11-12T14:12:05Z :white_check_mark:

marta: RBAC question — should the encryptor service assume a single KEK role or per-tenant KEKs? Per-tenant gives better blast radius but more complexity in key management and KMS calls.

tyler: Start with tenant-scoped KEKs for high-risk tenants only. Use a policy: service principal can only Decrypt for keys in allowed list. Keep a mapping in our authz store and verify at runtime. For Azure, map service principal to Key Vault access policies.

amanda: Incident playbook item — on KMS outage fallback: have a read-only degraded mode that serves from GRPC cache (if allowed) and rejects key creation/rotation ops. Add a feature flag to force fail-open vs fail-closed per tenant risk profile.

marta: Good. Last: any guidance on sampling KMS unwraps for telemetry to control throttling? We shouldn't sample only failures — need health metrics.

tyler: Sample >0.1% of success unwraps for deep tracing, and 100% of errors. Also log histogram of latency. Use adaptive sampling: increase sample rate if error rate or lat spikes above thresholds.

amanda: I'll draft a short runbook and the telemetry schema. Linking it here when ready.

marta: Thanks — that helps. I'll update the design doc with cache warmup + audit correlation approach and share for review.
